10.0.0.en: Christ chose twelve of His followers to become His disciples, and this calling came in stages. The goal was that they should be discipled at His hands, so that He would hand over to them the spiritual life and the teachings that they were to convey to the world and preach.

10.0.1.en: And as they went out to preach repentance and the Kingdom of Heaven, He strengthened them with authority to cast out demons and heal diseases, to help people believe their words, since the devil who dominates them is driven away from them, and they are relieved of their troubles, so that their hearts are more ready to receive the good news.

10.0.2.en: Offer your love to people, and their hearts will open and respond to your words.

10.1.0.en: The number of the disciples was twelve, that is, three times four, and it signifies the work of the Holy Trinity in the whole world with its four directions, and that they might preach to the twelve tribes of the Jews.

10.1.1.en: "Simon, who is called Peter": that is, a rock, or Cephas, and he was the first of the disciples and the eldest in age.

10.1.2.en: "Andrew": the brother of Simon Peter, and both of them had been disciples of John the Baptist.

10.1.3.en: "James the son of Zebedee": the first of the disciples to be martyred.

10.1.4.en: "John": the brother of James, and the two were sharp in temperament, so Christ called them "Boanerges," that is, sons of thunder. John was distinguished by his intense love for Christ, and he used to lean on His breast.

10.2.0.en: "Philip": from Bethsaida, and he is not Philip the evangelist, one of the seven deacons. He called Bartholomew, who is also called Nathanael, and who was from Cana of Galilee.

10.2.2.en: "Matthew": who is called Levi, and Matthew called himself the publican out of humility, because the tax collectors were known for their sins.

10.2.3.en: "James the son of Alphaeus": or James the Less, to distinguish him from James the son of Zebedee, who was older in age; he was a cousin of Christ on His mother's side, and he became bishop of Jerusalem.

10.2.4.en: "Lebbaeus": who is surnamed Thaddaeus, and is also called Judas; he was the son of Alphaeus, the brother of James, and he is the writer of the epistle known by his name (James).

10.3.0.en: "Simon the Canaanite": that is, the Zealot, and it does not mean that he was from Cana of Galilee. The Zealots were a group of Jews who held fast to their nationalism against the Roman authority, and were ready for acts of sabotage in defense of their Jewish homeland.

10.3.1.en: "Judas Iscariot": which means "man of Kerioth," one of the towns of Judea; he is the one who sold Christ to the Jews and delivered Him to them.

10.3.2.en: It is to be noted that Christ chose His disciples from ordinary people, and not from the eminent, so that their works would be ascribed to the power of God working in them and not to their personal strength; He is ready to accept and work through any person, however weak he may be.

10.3.3.en: And He chose them with differing temperaments: among them one who collaborated with the Roman authority, such as Matthew the tax collector, and also one who defied this authority, namely Simon the Zealot; among them the poor, such as Peter and Andrew, and the rich, such as James and John the sons of Zebedee. So He gathers all in His Church with one love.

10.3.4.en: God is ready to work in the least and weakest of people, so hold fast to your spiritual relationship with God, however weak you are before your sins, or however few your resources, because God is able to work through you, so that you serve Him, and the glory is to God through your thanking Him at all times.

10.4.0.en: Christ sent them to the land of Judea to preach in it, and not to Samaria, that is, the part split off from the Jews and mixed with the Gentiles and pagan worship. He likewise forbade them to go to the Gentiles, that is, the pagan lands, because Christ is the Messiah awaited by the Jews, who came for their salvation, so that everyone who awaited the divine promises and prophecies might believe in Him, and then the rest of the world would be evangelized. He came for the salvation of all, but He begins with the Jews, for they were supposed to be the first to respond to His good news, so that He might gather those of them who had strayed from the truth, then the Samaritans as a link between the Jews and the Gentiles, then the Gentiles; that is, in the end He offers salvation to all, and this is what happened after His Ascension (ch. 28:19).

10.5.0.en: The subject of the Apostles' preaching is the same as that preached by John the Baptist and by Christ Himself, namely repentance in preparation for the Kingdom of Heaven, because through repentance a person rejects his sins and begins the new life with Christ, who then reigns over his heart, as a pledge of his enjoying the eternal Kingdom with Him.

10.6.0.en: Christ gave His disciples the means for preaching, which is authority to heal diseases, even difficult ones such as leprosy, which represents uncleanness. Indeed He gave them authority to raise the dead, and to cast demons out of the weak in soul; that is, He gave them authority over everything, even what seems impossible, in order to rescue His children from the hand of the devil, and to prepare them to receive the good news about Him.

10.6.1.en: And He required of them that their service be free of charge, as love without return, just as He gave them everything freely, so that they too might give to others, and hearts would be drawn to them.

10.6.2.en: And this is a principle that still holds in service to this day, namely that servants offer spiritual service without payment.

10.7.0.en: Gold, silver, brass: money at that time was made of these three metals, so what is meant is any kind of money or any pieces of these metals that have monetary value. Since Christ strengthens them with His power, they do not need to take money with them, or food in their scrips, that is, the bags that they carry on a journey, and they do not need clothes or shoes, or a staff to lean on, because Christ is their support; and if they need these things He will provide them through those to whom they preach, because, although the service is free, the servant's necessary needs can be provided by God for him through the gifts of those he serves.

10.7.1.en: What is meant here is that the disciple should be content with the necessary needs that he uses, and not take with him anything extra as a precaution, because if any of them is lost, God will provide it for him.

10.8.0.en: Christ charged them that, if they entered any place to preach in it, they should look for those who respond to the word of God or are ready to hear the word; these are the ones worthy to receive the good news, so that they repent and amend their lives. And He told them to keep staying in that responsive house, so that they might complete the persuasion of the responsive ones until they draw them to Him; they should not move quickly from house to house, but complete the persuasion and care of each person. On the other hand, they should not be occupied with hospitality and seek after it in different houses, because their aim is preaching, and the house in which they stay is merely a place to lodge, from which they set out to serve souls.

10.9.0.en: "Salute it": offer greetings, love and sufficient care to the people of the house, for preaching is not a dry work, but is accompanied by feelings of love; and the importance of expressing feelings in order to draw people appears here.

10.9.1.en: Christ commanded them to proclaim His peace to all hearts, and to offer their love to all. If some respond, they will enjoy the salvation of Christ, and benefit from the peace offered to them. And if they refuse, the disciples should not grieve, for their peace and love return to them, while those who refuse lose the grace of God.

10.10.0.en: "Shake off the dust of your feet": shaking off dust was a well-known custom, signifying the clearing of responsibility, since the Apostles had done what was upon them, and those who refuse are therefore held accountable for their rejection of the word of God. It also signifies taking nothing material from these who refuse, not even the dust on the feet.

10.11.0.en: "The day of judgment": it is the last day of judgment.

10.11.1.en: But those who reject the good news of Christ at the hands of the Apostles will lose their opportunity to reach the Kingdom and the redemption of Christ, and will be cast into eternal torment, and their torment will be harder than the torment of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, who were known for their wickedness in ancient times, to the point that God burned the two cities (Gen 19:24), because in the Old Testament they rejected the words of the men of God. But in the New Testament they rejected Christ Himself.

10.11.2.en: Take care to express your love for those around you every day, and for all whom you serve and wish to draw to Christ, for expressing love in word and deed is the necessary preparation for opening hearts to obey the word of God, since they see Him in you and so submit to His word that is on your lips.

10.12.s.en: (3) The world's persecution of the disciples

10.12.0.en: If one wolf among the lambs terrifies them, although it will devour only some of them, how great would the terror be if we placed lambs among many wolves? But so that the power of God may be manifested in the weak lambs, they are placed among the wolves and overcome them, and strip them of their savage nature. And even if the wolves devour the lambs, the blood of the lambs will run in the veins of the wolves and turn them into lambs, as St. John Chrysostom says.

10.12.1.en: And this is what actually happened during the preaching of the Apostles, who endured violent persecutions and changed many hard hearts, just as the martyrs drew to faith those who were tormenting them.

10.12.2.en: And Christ calls His disciples to be adorned with the simplicity and innocence of the dove, because it is known for not harming others. And at the same time, to be marked by the wisdom of serpents, which are known for their great caution against danger, so that we keep away from all evil in order to live with God.

10.13.0.en: "Beware": be on guard against the wicked whom you are preaching to, and do not throw yourselves into their hands without need; but if preaching requires it, do not be afraid.

10.13.1.en: "Councils": these are either the local councils of the elders of the Jews found in every village to pass judgments on wrongdoers, or the supreme council in Jerusalem, which is the "Sanhedrin" (ch. 5:21-22). "Their synagogues": they were spread throughout all the land of Judea, and in them the Holy Scriptures were read and preaching was given, and in them there were three judges from among the elders who had the right to pass sentences of flogging on offenders.

10.13.2.en: "They will scourge you": they used to scourge offenders with forty lashes, and as a precaution, lest they err, the Jews fixed it at 39 lashes, since the whip is made of three strands, so the offender was lashed 13 times, which equals 39 lashes.

10.13.3.en: "Governors and kings": who tried the Apostles, such as Felix the governor (Acts 24), and Agrippa the king (Acts 26), who both tried St. Paul the Apostle.

10.13.4.en: "A testimony for them": that they might believe, as Paul tried with King Agrippa (Acts 26).

10.13.5.en: "To the Gentiles": that is, all the crowds who listen to their trial, as many of them believed during the trial and torture of the martyrs.

10.13.6.en: Here Christ speaks in detail about the kinds of persecutions that will meet the Apostles, or the children of God in every generation: instead of honoring them in appreciation of their preaching, they will arrest them and try them, and torture them with scourging and with many kinds of torments, and this will be a proof of the faith of the servants and their steadfastness in Christ.

10.14.0.en: Christ reassures us in these confrontations that the Holy Spirit will give us what to answer them, so that we persuade them or silence them, because the power of the Holy Spirit in us is stronger than all human wisdom. "The Spirit of your Father": it shows the tenderness and care of God, who makes His Holy Spirit support the Apostles and servants in every generation.

10.15.0.en: Persecutions will come, not only from those who are far off, but from the nearest people, such as father, child and brother, and it is strange that religious fanaticism abolishes natural love between the nearest of the near, but this is what has happened and does happen to this day.

10.16.0.en: "All men": most of the people who do not believe in Christ.

10.16.1.en: "For my name's sake": for your holding fast to the faith and to preaching.

10.16.2.en: "Endureth": persecution does not mean killing only, but mostly insult, torture and deprivation of rights, and so it requires the patience of the servants and the believers.

10.16.3.en: "The end": the end of the persecution or the end of life.

10.16.4.en: Tribulation may reach the point where a person finds everyone around him hating and persecuting him for the sake of Christ, and God will allow this to prove our faith. And by patience and endurance we gain the salvation of our souls, and even an eternal reward that cannot be expressed, with the assurance that the Holy Spirit supports us so that we may endure these persecutions.

10.17.0.en: Christ counsels His Apostles not to enter into confrontations with the wicked, if they refuse to believe, but to flee to other lands, and complete their preaching. This fleeing is not weakness, but busyness with completing the preaching, as proved by the fact that in the end they accepted martyrdom for the sake of Christ with joy; all the disciples were martyred except John, who endured many torments and was exiled and died in exile.

10.17.1.en: And Christ gives them the good news that they will not complete their preaching until He comes and reigns over the hearts of people through their faith in Him, that is, until the preaching spreads in the whole world.

10.17.2.en: Likewise the Temple was destroyed in AD 70, as a proclamation of the end of Jewish worship and the spread of Christianity as the new Israel.

10.17.3.en: Hold fast to your principles of self-giving love like the lamb ready for slaughter, of simplicity and not harming others like the dove, in addition to wisdom in offering this love at the right time and in the right way, so that you may show Christ to everyone you meet, confident that the power of God in you is stronger than the world and its evil: love overcomes hatred, and simplicity overcomes cunning, because the God who is in you protects you and guides you, so that you go forward toward all hard hearts and soften them and bring them back to God.

10.18.0.en: "The disciple is not above his master": the disciples of Christ are not better than He; if Christ was subjected to insults and the Cross, it is natural that they share His sufferings by enduring persecutions. "Nor the servant above his lord": it appears that these sayings were well known at that time, and Christ took them to point to His meaning; the servant means the believers, and the lord is Christ.

10.18.1.en: "Beelzebub": he is the god of the Ekronites (the people of a city in Palestine), a land neighboring the Jews (2 Kgs 1:2), and his original name is Baal-zebub, that is, the god of flies, because they believed he drove the flies away from them, and the Jews called him Beelzebul in contempt of him.

10.18.2.en: "They of his household": that is, the disciples and those who believe in Christ, who are His children and members in His Church, which is His house. Christ reminds His disciples that the world will persecute Him, and will say of Him that He is the prince of the devils, and consequently they will persecute them because they are His disciples, and their carrying of the Cross is a proof of their following Him.

10.19.0.en: "Covered... hid": these are all the teachings of Christ that they learned in the house with Him, or that only the Jewish people knew.

10.19.1.en: "Revealed": appears and reaches all the Gentiles.

10.19.2.en: "Darkness": quiet places with dim light, or the sittings of Christ with His disciples in secret during the night.

10.19.3.en: "Light": it means open proclamation and preaching before all.

10.19.4.en: "Ear": what the disciples heard in private sittings with Christ.

10.19.5.en: "Housetops": what is meant is teaching and preaching from pulpits, or high places, so that all may hear it. Christ warns them not to fear people's accusations against them, because their service and their love of righteousness will appear and be made known in time before all, and their preaching of Christ will reach all the earth, and by this He gives the first reason for not fearing enemies. And He encouraged them to preach everywhere with boldness and power, and what they heard from Him in quiet sittings, they should proclaim to people in a loud voice from the housetops everywhere, and thus the preaching spreads so that all may believe.

10.20.0.en: Christ gives a second reason for not fearing people, which is that the most that the authority of men can reach is to harm the body, but the spirit they cannot harm. But the One who deserves to be feared is God, who has authority over both spirit and body; if we fear God, we will not fear people.

10.21.0.en: The farthing: the smallest known Jewish coin.

10.21.1.en: Here He gives the third reason for not fearing people, which is God's care for us and His concern for all creatures. The sparrow, one of the smallest birds, whose price is half a farthing, God cares for its needs, and it does not die except by His permission. How much more does God care for man, the head of all creation, and even for the smallest thing in man, which is his hair, which is not only numbered but counted by God, that is, every hair has a number with Him and does not fall except by His permission.

10.21.2.en: Rely on God and go forth in His service, assured that He protects you and keeps you and arranges your whole life, for He is responsible for you, and Satan is afraid to come near you because of the God who supports you.

10.22.0.en: "Confess me": shows My name in his words and conduct, holding fast to the commandments, and rejecting sin by repentance.

10.22.1.en: "My Father which is in heaven": I cover him with My mercy and intercede for him with My blood and bring him into the heavenly glories. For our entering into the divine justice, which is the Father, is through the mercy of the Son. The fourth reason for not fearing is the heavenly reward: everyone who stands firm in his faith and preaches in His name, confessing Him before the world, He will declare His care for him in heaven. But whoever rejects Him on earth and keeps away from Him, God will reject him in heaven.

10.23.0.en: "A sword": that is, the conflict between good and evil, or the persecution of the followers of Christ by unbelievers, so there is no outward peace, but God grants them His inner peace during persecutions.

10.23.1.en: "The daughter in law": the wife of the son.

10.23.2.en: Christ declares the suffering that a person endures in order to hold fast to the faith, that is, the Cross that he bears for the sake of Christ.

10.23.3.en: And He also called it a sword, since because of faith problems occur inside the one family, so the father persecutes his son because he believed in Christ, and likewise the pagan mother persecutes her Christian daughter... and so the Christian finds hostility from the members of his household; and for the sake of Christ he endures all these pains.

10.24.0.en: If human affections are strong within the one family, our love for Christ is greater than any affection. So if the faith of those close to us conflicts with our faith in Christ, we must obey God, otherwise we do not deserve to have Him as God, and we have no place with Him in heaven; for God must be obeyed rather than men.

10.25.0.en: Whoever wants to be a follower of Christ must endure pains for His sake, and give up much as a proof of his love for Him.

10.26.0.en: "He that findeth his life": that is, he is busy with the lusts of the world, and finds his pleasure in them.

10.26.1.en: "Shall lose it": that is, he takes it away from God, so it finds no place in heaven, but in eternal perdition. "Loseth his life": he gives his life in the toils of worship and service.

10.26.2.en: "Shall find it": he receives peace and consolation and fellowship with God on earth, then the eternal reward in the heavens. Christ asks us to give up our comfort and our bodily pleasures for His sake, and whoever gives them up finds true rest in Him, and even receives complete rest in eternity.

10.26.3.en: Look at what you have left for the sake of Christ as a proof of your love for Him, and hold fast to His commandments even if you lose some material things in which others delight, for being with Christ is better than evil pleasures or laziness and ease.

10.27.0.en: "Him that sent me": that is, God, for receiving the teachings of Christ on earth is receiving the God whom the Jews know.

10.27.1.en: "In the name of a prophet": that is, as being a prophet, and not for his person. For a person may be ordinary, but the gift of prophecy raises his rank, like the honor of the priest, however weak his person and his former standing were before the priesthood. "A prophet's reward": that is, God's blessing for the prophet or for whoever honors the prophet.

10.27.2.en: "Righteous man": a believer who lives in godliness and spirituality.

10.27.3.en: As encouragement from Christ to His disciples in the face of persecutions, He declares their dignity, and that honoring them is honoring Him personally, and receiving their word is receiving Him, and consequently everyone who receives them is rewarded with a divine reward.

10.28.0.en: "Little ones": the servants who endure many toils in serving Him and conveying His word to people.

10.28.1.en: "A cup of cold water": that is, the least refreshing drink, which helps the servants to continue their service.

10.28.2.en: "In the name of a disciple": as being a disciple, or as a follower of Christ.

10.28.3.en: "In no wise lose his reward": that is, he has a heavenly reward.

10.28.4.en: Christ shows the importance of the smallest service offered to the servants of God, even if it is a cup of cold water, for whoever offers it will receive his reward from God. For if the servants or priests or bishops give spiritual care to their people, then the flock ought to show its love for God in their persons, by working for their comfort, or providing their needs, as a declaration of their love for God, who, in His humility, offers Himself to them through these servants. If someone offers a cup of water to the servant, considering him a disciple of Christ, God will surely reward him in heaven, and even in his life on earth.

10.28.5.en: Do not belittle your love which you offer to God in gladdening those around you, however small it seems, such as words of encouragement or material help and psychological support, for it is precious in God's sight, and He will reward you for it. If you find an opportunity to serve, do not neglect it, and look for what you can give to everyone you meet, especially those close to you.

10.28.6.en: The discourse about John the Baptist, the rejection of faith
